short_description: An enveloped gammaretrovirus (~80-100 nm) that infects the blood-forming cells of the bone marrow and spreads through mutual grooming, shared bowls and saliva. Unlike its sibling FIV (a lentivirus with a CONE-shaped core), FeLV is a classic 'C-type' particle: barely-visible short Env spikes over the envelope, and a roughly SPHERICAL, centrally-placed condensed core (capsid p27) that assembles at the plasma membrane at the same moment it buds off.
taxonomy: Family Retroviridae, genus Gammaretrovirus (distinct from FIV, a Lentivirus; both are feline-specific retroviruses but with different genome organisation, protein nomenclature and core morphology).

do_not_draw: A conical / cone-shaped core - that is the sibling render FIV (and HIV), both lentiviruses. FeLV is a GAMMAretrovirus and its core is roughly SPHERICAL / isometric and centrally placed - the single most checkable, most confusable feature between the two adjacent atlas entries.
A non-enveloped / naked particle - FeLV is always enveloped in a host-derived lipid bilayer.
A faceted, geometric icosahedral capsid drawn like a soccer-ball / adenovirus - the C-type core reads as a smooth, dense, roughly spherical body, not a polyhedral shell with visible facets.
A double-stranded DNA genome inside the virion - the packaged genome is TWO COPIES of positive-sense single-stranded RNA (it only becomes DNA after reverse transcription inside the host cell).

Long, prominent, mushroom/club-stalked spikes copied from a coronavirus or HIV render - ICTV explicitly describes Gammaretrovirus surface spikes as 'barely visible'; FeLV's Env knobs must read as short and sparse, not tall clubs or a dense fuzzy corona.
A bullet-shaped silhouette with a flat and a rounded end - that is rabies (a rhabdovirus, also in this set), not FeLV; FeLV is roughly spherical.
A cat, a person, or any animal figure in the four science styles (sem/textbook/3d/watercolor) - those are molecule-scale renders of the virion alone.
Anything implying human infectivity - FeLV cannot infect people; it is a cat-specific virus.
verification_note: Core shape confirmed as SPHERICAL / centrally-placed ('C-type' morphology), NOT conical, per the ICTV Genus: Gammaretrovirus report and the ICTV Virus Taxonomy Profile: Retroviridae 2021 (which explicitly contrasts 'concentric' (Gammaretrovirus, along with Alpha-/Deltaretrovirus) cores against 'rod or truncated cone-shaped' (Lentivirus, i.e. FIV/HIV) cores) - checked explicitly against the FIV sibling render on every accepted render (see render.md §5).

sources.claim: Genus Gammaretrovirus: 'Virions exhibit a "C-type" morphology with barely visible surface spikes. They have a centrally located, condensed core. Capsid assembly occurs at the inner surface of the membrane at the same time as budding.' - the direct, explicit statement that FeLV's core (as a gammaretrovirus) is a roughly spherical, centrally-placed condensed body, not a cone.

Family Retroviridae: virions are spherical, enveloped, 80-100 nm in diameter, with glycoprotein surface projections ~8 nm long, irregularly spaced. The apparently spherical nucleocapsid (nucleoid) is 'concentric' (i.e. centred) for genera Alpharetrovirus, Gammaretrovirus and Deltaretrovirus, but 'rod or truncated cone-shaped' for genus Lentivirus (which includes FIV and HIV) - the explicit taxonomic contrast between FeLV's spherical core and FIV's conical core.
sources.source: Krupovic et al., ICTV Virus Taxonomy Profile: Retroviridae 2021, J Gen Virol 102:001712

sources.claim: FeLV gag gene codes for the viral structural core proteins p15 (matrix), p10 (nucleocapsid), and p12 and p27 (capsid); pol gene encodes p14 (protease), p80 (reverse transcriptase) and p46 (integrase); env gene encodes the surface glycoprotein gp70 and the transmembrane protein p15E. p27 is the major capsid protein and the standard diagnostic antigen-test target.
sources.source: Ferrero et al., Feline Leukemia Virus in Cats: A Novel Rapid ELISA Assay for p27 Antigen Detection, Veterinary Medicine International 2025 (open access, CC BY)

sources.claim: FeLV core/capsid composed of capsid protein p27 with a surrounding matrix (p15), enclosed by a phospholipid envelope bearing gp70 (surface) and p15E (transmembrane) Env proteins; genome carries two identical RNA strands plus reverse transcriptase, integrase and protease packaged in the core - confirms the same gene-product naming and packaging pattern independently.
sources.source: Feline Leukemia Virus Infection, in Canine and Feline Infectious Diseases (Sykes & Hartmann, 2014) / summarised in veterinary reference compilations
